title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of passenger cars and light commercial vehicles with regard to the protection of the occupants of the front seats in the event of a frontal collision, with focus on the restraint system (restraint system in front impact), version 4.0.0 (04 series of amendments)
scope_summary: Approves vehicle types with regard to the protection of front-seat occupants in a full-width frontal collision against a rigid barrier at 50 km/h, assessed with Hybrid III 50th percentile male (driver) and 5th percentile female (passenger) dummies. The approval also covers post-crash requirements such as electrical safety of high-voltage systems and REESS, and hydrogen leakage, and applies to M1 vehicles of up to 3,500 kg and all N1 vehicles.
scope_quote: This Regulation applies to vehicles of category M1 with a maximum permissible mass not exceeding 3,500 kg and to vehicles of category N1.
vehicle_categories: M1 (maximum permissible mass not exceeding 3,500 kg)
applies_to_components: Protective system (interior fittings and devices intended to restrain the occupants)
Safety belts and restraint systems of front seats
Airbags, including passenger airbags, and their user instructions/warnings
Vehicle structure forward of the transverse plane through the driver's R point
Doors and automatically activated door locking systems (post-crash opening)
Electric power train, high voltage bus and high voltage live parts (post-crash electrical safety)
Electrical protection barriers, enclosures and solid insulators
Electrical energy conversion systems (e.g. fuel cell) and electronic converters
Coupling system for charging the REESS
Compressed hydrogen storage system (container, container attachments, shut-off valve) and downstream piping
Engine siting/orientation and fuel system as relevant to impact behaviour
relation_to_other_regulations: Vehicle categories M1 and N1 as defined in the Consolidated Resolution on the Construction of Vehicles (R.E.3), ECE/TRANS/WP.29/78/Rev.7
R point and H point determination per Addendum 6 of Mutual Resolution No. 1 (M.R.1) (Annex 6)
Approval numbering per Schedule 4 of the 1958 Agreement (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3)
Hydrogen fuel specified by ISO 14687:2019 and SAE J2719_202003
04 series of amendments extends the 03 series AF05 thorax compression limit (ThCC 34 mm) from M1 to a certain range of N1 vehicles
Approval mark may be combined with marks of other UN Regulations under which the vehicle is approved (para. 4.5)

defined_terms.label: Protective system
defined_terms.definition: Interior fittings and devices intended to restrain the occupants and contribute towards ensuring compliance with the requirements of paragraph 5.

defined_terms.label: Type of protective system
defined_terms.definition: A category of protective devices which do not differ in technology, geometry or constituent materials.

defined_terms.label: Vehicle width
defined_terms.definition: Distance between two planes parallel to the longitudinal median plane touching the vehicle on either side, excluding indirect vision devices, lamps, tyre pressure indicators, flexible mud-guards and deflected tyre side-walls.

defined_terms.label: Vehicle type
defined_terms.definition: Power-driven vehicles not differing in length/width, front structure, passenger compartment and protective system, engine siting, unladen mass, optional fittings, REESS location and CHSS configuration insofar as they adversely affect the impact test.

defined_terms.label: Passenger compartment with regard to occupant protection
defined_terms.definition: Space for occupant accommodation bounded by roof, floor, side walls, doors, outside glazing, front bulkhead and the rear compartment bulkhead or rear-seat back support plane.

defined_terms.label: Passenger compartment for electric safety and/or hydrogen safety assessment
defined_terms.definition: Occupant space bounded by roof, floor, side walls, doors, glazing, front and rear bulkhead or back door, and the electrical protection barriers and enclosures protecting from direct contact with high voltage live parts.

defined_terms.label: R point
defined_terms.definition: Reference point defined for each seat by the manufacturer in relation to the vehicle structure, as indicated in Annex 6.

defined_terms.label: H point
defined_terms.definition: Reference point determined for each seat by the testing service per the procedure in Annex 6.

defined_terms.label: Unladen kerb mass
defined_terms.definition: Mass of the vehicle in running order, unoccupied and unladen but complete with fuel, coolant, lubricant, tools and spare wheel if standard.

defined_terms.label: Airbag
defined_terms.definition: A device supplementing safety belts and restraint systems which in a severe impact automatically deploys a flexible gas-filled structure to limit the gravity of occupant contacts with the passenger compartment interior.

defined_terms.label: Passenger airbag
defined_terms.definition: An airbag assembly intended to protect occupant(s) in seats other than the driver's in a frontal collision.

defined_terms.label: High voltage
defined_terms.definition: Classification of an electric component or circuit with working voltage > 60 V and ≤ 1,500 V DC or > 30 V and ≤ 1,000 V AC rms.

defined_terms.label: Rechargeable Electrical Energy Storage System (REESS)
defined_terms.definition: Rechargeable energy storage system providing electric energy for electrical propulsion, excluding batteries primarily for starting, lighting or auxiliaries.

defined_terms.label: Electrical protection barrier
defined_terms.definition: The part providing protection against any direct contact to the high voltage live parts.

defined_terms.label: Electric power train
defined_terms.definition: Electrical circuit including the traction motor(s) and possibly the REESS, energy conversion system, electronic converters, wiring harness, connectors and charging coupling system.

defined_terms.label: Live parts
defined_terms.definition: Conductive part(s) intended to be electrically energized under normal operating conditions.

defined_terms.label: Exposed conductive part
defined_terms.definition: Conductive part touchable under IPXXB, not normally energized but which can become energized under isolation failure, including parts under tool-less removable covers.

defined_terms.label: Protection degree IPXXB
defined_terms.definition: Protection from contact with high voltage live parts by an electrical protection barrier or enclosure, tested with the Jointed Test Finger per Annex 9 para. 4.

defined_terms.label: Working voltage
defined_terms.definition: Highest rms circuit voltage specified by the manufacturer which may occur between conductive parts in open circuit or normal operation, defined per galvanically isolated circuit.

defined_terms.label: Coupling system for charging the REESS
defined_terms.definition: Electrical circuit used for charging the REESS from an external power supply including the vehicle inlet.

defined_terms.label: Electrical chassis
defined_terms.definition: Set of electrically linked conductive parts whose potential is taken as reference.

defined_terms.label: Electrical circuit
defined_terms.definition: Assembly of connected live parts designed to be electrically energized in normal operation.

defined_terms.label: Electrical energy conversion system
defined_terms.definition: A system (e.g. fuel cell) that generates and provides electrical energy for electrical propulsion.

defined_terms.label: Electronic converter
defined_terms.definition: A device capable of controlling and/or converting electrical power for electrical propulsion.

defined_terms.label: Enclosure
defined_terms.definition: The part enclosing internal units and providing protection against any direct contact.

defined_terms.label: High voltage bus
defined_terms.definition: Electrical circuit, including the REESS charging coupling system, operating on high voltage.

defined_terms.label: Solid insulator
defined_terms.definition: Insulating coating of wiring harnesses covering high voltage live parts against direct contact.

defined_terms.label: Automatic disconnect
defined_terms.definition: A device that when triggered galvanically separates the electrical energy sources from the rest of the high voltage circuit of the electric power train.

defined_terms.label: Open type traction battery
defined_terms.definition: A battery requiring filling with liquid and generating hydrogen gas released to the atmosphere.

defined_terms.label: Automatically activated door locking system
defined_terms.definition: A system that locks the doors automatically at a preset speed or under other manufacturer-defined conditions.

defined_terms.label: Displacement system
defined_terms.definition: A device by which the seat or its parts can be displaced and/or rotated without fixed intermediate position to permit access to the space behind the seat.

defined_terms.label: Aqueous electrolyte
defined_terms.definition: Electrolyte based on water solvent providing conducting ions after dissociation.

defined_terms.label: Electrolyte leakage
defined_terms.definition: Escape of electrolyte from the REESS in liquid form.

defined_terms.label: Non-aqueous electrolyte
defined_terms.definition: Electrolyte not based on water as the solvent.

defined_terms.label: Specific voltage condition
defined_terms.definition: Condition where the maximum voltage of a galvanically connected circuit between a DC live part and any other live part is ≤ 30 V AC rms and ≤ 60 V DC.

defined_terms.label: State of Charge (SOC)
defined_terms.definition: Available electrical charge in a REESS as a percentage of its rated capacity.

defined_terms.label: Fire
defined_terms.definition: Emission of flames from the vehicle, excluding sparks and arcing.

defined_terms.label: Explosion
defined_terms.definition: Sudden release of energy sufficient to cause pressure waves and/or projectiles that may damage the vehicle surroundings.

defined_terms.label: Compressed hydrogen storage system (CHSS)
defined_terms.definition: System storing compressed hydrogen fuel, composed of a container, container attachments and all primary closure devices isolating stored hydrogen.

defined_terms.label: Container (for hydrogen storage)
defined_terms.definition: Pressure-bearing component storing the primary volume of hydrogen fuel in one or multiple permanently interconnected chambers.

defined_terms.label: Container attachments
defined_terms.definition: Non-pressure bearing parts attached to the container providing support/protection, removable only with tools for maintenance/inspection.

defined_terms.label: Hydrogen-fuelled vehicle
defined_terms.definition: Motor vehicle using compressed gaseous hydrogen as fuel for propulsion, including fuel cell and internal combustion engine vehicles.

defined_terms.label: Shut-off valve (for hydrogen-fuelled vehicles)
defined_terms.definition: Valve between the container and vehicle fuel system that defaults to closed when not connected to a power source.

applicability_hints: This is a whole-vehicle approval; components (seat belts, airbags, steering wheels, seats, dashboards, knee bolsters, pretensioners/load limiters) are not separately approved but are assessed as part of the 'protective system' and can affect the vehicle type definition
Any change to the structure forward of the driver's R point, front-end crash structures, engine siting/orientation or unladen mass can require extension/re-test
Airbag modules (driver and passenger) trigger the user instruction and warning requirements of para. 6
Seats with easy-entry displacement systems and automatically activated door locking systems are subject to post-crash requirements (door opening, seat locking)

Battery-electric, hybrid and fuel-cell vehicles: high voltage components (REESS, inverters/electronic converters, HV cables, connectors, charging inlet, automatic disconnect, protection barriers/enclosures) must meet post-crash electrical safety, isolation and electrolyte leakage requirements; REESS location is part of the vehicle type
12 V/48 V starting/auxiliary batteries are not REESS and circuits under the specific voltage condition are not high voltage bus

Hydrogen-fuelled vehicles: CHSS, containers, container attachments, shut-off valves and downstream piping are subject to post-crash leak and enclosed-space concentration limits; CHSS configuration is part of the vehicle type
Small N1 vans/trucks fall under the 04 series AF05 thorax limit, not only passenger cars
Optional fittings offered by the manufacturer can create a different vehicle type if they adversely affect the impact result
